blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Use one current AI success and frustration to frame the seven short reasoning checks. Record explanations and move quickly through sound answers.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Compare three firm tasks, then map calculation, classification, retrieval and drafting to their different mechanisms.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Predict the consent answer, run it, read KT-1 together and mark the unconfirmed transaction trigger.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Choose one firm task, describe today's process and evidence owner, then write a success test together.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Choose a proposed pilot task and explain who would review its output.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Change the example to a deadline reminder. Ask for a mechanism, a failure test and a two-sentence explanation to a partner.

title: How AI learns and represents information

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Explain training and inference using yesterday's contract example before showing a definition.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Walk through labelled documents, the training loop and held-out evaluation. Then compare token IDs, embeddings and contextual representations.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Predict which sentence pairs will be close, inspect actual cosine values and compare a consent sentence with its opposite.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Use a short document-label check, then test held-out evaluation, near-duplicate leakage and why similarity cannot settle consent.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: List evidence a vendor would need to show beyond a falling training-loss curve.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Give charge a new context and explain the changed meaning. Check whether uploading a file retrains the model.

title: How language models generate answers and fail

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Recall how inference differs from training. Ask which parts of today's answer are still unknown.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Build token generation and context examples, then distinguish unsupported facts, missing evidence and valid variation.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Run one fresh response and compare the saved dated repeats and evidence scopes. Prioritise the missing-fee and release checks.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Mark the failed response, apply the review workflow and compare the revised answer. Then change only the transaction to a share sale.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Agree what must be checked before a draft can enter the matter file.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Explain why a repeated answer is not independent verification. Separate a raw run, a revision after feedback and an instructor answer.

title: AI tools, effective instructions and safe use

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Recall a correct citation that still failed to support the conclusion.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Compare available tool roles, practise briefing a junior colleague and inspect the teaching account's data-use questions.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Start with the learner’s usual AI brief, then compare a review specification on the same evidence. Inspect support and review effort.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Add one missing acceptance test, inspect a revision and test Variant A. Decide what belongs in the repeatable firm review process.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Record the tool decision, an unanswered procurement question and the approval owner.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Explain what additional evidence a paid account does and does not supply about employer-data permission.

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Name the data format, modality and source system for three law-firm examples.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Trace a scanned contract through OCR, correction, structured records, bounded chunks and an index. Locate the access checks.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Compare clean and degraded OCR, then inspect the source sentence whose negation was lost.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Complete an inventory row, inspect the oversized-chunk diagnostic, preserve KT-1 and its context, then assign a correction owner.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Choose a collection to prepare and define the quality gate before indexing it.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Change the example to a scanned tax schedule. Explain which relationships and source locations must survive conversion.

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Recall the difference between a readable file, a searchable index and a supported answer.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Explain retrieval and generation separately, then trace token limits, source purpose, document identity, ranking and amendment context.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Compare the original failed search with bounded chunks and the repaired evidence packet. Read the retrieved rule and its exception.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Choose a new query and source purpose, test a paraphrase, request an unavailable agreement and compare a consent statement with its opposite.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Record separate acceptance gates for retrieval, answer fidelity and permissions.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Explain why all eight fixture checks passing does not prove production reliability. Identify one additional representative firm test.

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Recall why a relevant-looking hit is still only a candidate source.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Set the historical research scope, distinguish submissions from findings and identify statute editions and page pinpoints.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Inspect the failed report, add page 1's actual four rows and compare its claims with pages 3 and 22–24 of the original judgment.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Build three claim records, draft a short historical note and separate current-law questions. Record the conflicting Tribunal year without guessing.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Agree which claims can be released and which need a further source or qualified review.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Inspect a genuine citation that does not establish the proposition. Explain the limit of a search returning no later appellate decision.

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Recall the transaction-trigger check and distinguish an assignment from a share sale.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Read the party, obligation and source-version records. Trace the Key Terms override and relevant cross-references.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Repair the flawed review using the complete clause. Distinguish a source quotation from a proposed customer-side amendment.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Apply Variant B, review share-sale remedies including materiality, cure and liability exceptions, then draft and explain one amendment.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Record the reviewer's decision and what still needs source evidence or legal research.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Change only continued responsibility, leaving control unknown. Explain why an exception failure alone does not establish the trigger.

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Recall which part of the system approves an action and which part drafts a recommendation.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Compare RPA, defined workflows and tool-selecting agents. Trace a lookup, host decision and human review boundary.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Inspect the successful private Zapier test, then a real model-selected lookup trace. State which part demonstrates tool choice.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Test unknown ID, injected instructions and the call limit. Then approve, change and reject a local mock action while I operate the tools.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Choose a read-only pilot scope, permitted tools and a stop condition with a proposed owner.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Separate model cooperation from host enforcement. Review an accurate lookup followed by an unsupported legal inference.

title: Tax evidence workflows and controlled actions

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Recall why a valid receipt reference alone does not establish tax treatment.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Separate source-file roles, accounting reconciliation, exception investigation and authority to declare or submit.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Recalculate the reconciliation, compare the two saved prompts and inspect the official FDN guidance.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Work through the ledger challenge together for 25 minutes, then test uncertain acknowledgement and safe retry for 10 minutes.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Record missing evidence, the reviewer and the boundary between a preparation pack and formal submission.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Move one receipt to a different month. Recompute the effect before accepting the old conclusion.

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Recall the difference between an output error, an access incident and a data-retention concern.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Apply the risk framework to the recurring matter, then identify proportionate access, retention and incident controls.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Compare clean and difficult-scan OCR results and discuss which matters the difference may disadvantage.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Run the restricted-matter incident through containment, evidence preservation, recipient identification, review and restart conditions.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Draft one approved-use rule with owners, a reporting route and review conditions.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Change the incident from a retrieved paragraph to an email attachment. Explain which controls and evidence change.

title: Leading implementation and evaluating a pilot

blocks.label: Recall or entry diagnostic
blocks.action: Repeat selected entry concepts in new examples before opening the answer key.

blocks.label: Concepts and explanation
blocks.action: Explain pilot scope, critical failures, total review effort and the difference between capacity and cash savings.

blocks.label: Worked demonstration
blocks.action: Calculate the main cost case and stress case together. Identify assumptions that determine the result.

blocks.label: Break
blocks.action: Take a five-minute break.

blocks.label: Guided application and tests
blocks.action: Adapt one worked proposal to the learner's chosen task: baseline, sources, exclusions, tests, owners and day-30/60/90 decisions.

blocks.label: Firm decision and understanding
blocks.action: Complete the exit diagnostic and decide whether the proposal is ready for the firm's approval process.

blocks.label: Transfer and recap
blocks.action: Explain the proposal to a fellow partner in two minutes, then identify the next evidence request and review date.
